content.title: Chili’s viral post on Ruth’s Chris dress code sparks online debate
content.text: by: Ashley Suter Posted: Mar 25, 2026 / 08:56 AM EDT Updated: Mar 25, 2026 / 11:18 AM EDT TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA)— Chili’s spoke out on social media about Ruth’s Chris Steak House restaurant’s new dress code. Ruth’s Chris announced its dress code for eating at the restaurant, saying “business casual — proper attire required please.” The restaurant asked guests to remove all hats when entering. If guests are wearing ball caps, they will be asked to dine in the bar/lounge. Close-up of sign with logo on facade of Ruth’s Chris Steak House, Walnut Creek, California, August 25, 2025. (Photo by Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images) Ruth’s Chris also said the following attire is not allowed in the dining rooms: Gym wear Pool attire Tank tops Clothing with offensive graphics or language Revealing clothing or exposed undergarments With the new dress code, Chili’s spoke out about it on X, formerly known as Twitter, saying, “The only dress code at Chili’s is that you have to be dressed.” The now-viral post with 1.1 million views sparked a debate on dress codes at restaurants and whether the two are similar. A Chili’s Grill & Bar sign is visible in Orlando, Florida. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images) One user wrote under the post, “Chilis would never turn us away in times of need.” While another said, “Which is why Chili’s is Chili’s and Ruth’s Chris is Ruth’s Chris. Totally different vibe. Nothing wrong with either spot.”
